messages:
sam: quick datapoint — noticed a perf regression on A100 for seq_len=128 around 03:20 PST. kernel picker is choosing warp-specialized tile=64 path but end-to-end latency is up ~18% vs yesterday. suspects: reg pressure + smem spikes.
elaine: ugh. do you have the profile dump?
sam: pasted snippet from the pprof (trimmed):
```
Kernel: warp_tile_64_specialized  time: 12.4ms  regs: 64  smem: 48KB  active_warps: 10
Kernel: generic_tile_32            time: 9.8ms   regs: 48  smem: 24KB  active_warps: 16
Observed: more serial stalls on warp_tile_64, higher local memory usage (spill).
```
ryan: interesting — warp_specialized gives better parallelism when regs/smem allow high occupancy. here regs=64 looks tight on A100 40GB config. autotuner probably favored it due to per-kernel latency microbench (cold).
ryan: two quick hypotheses: 1) tile=64 uses more registers per thread -> lower occupancy -> slower on common seqlen/batch mix. 2) KV-prefetch added smem footprint so combined smem pushes block out of L1/SM balance -> more bank conflicts.
maria: can we reproduce with a tiny harness? run microbench across tile_sizes [32,48,64] + with/without kv-prefetch. if kv adds smem, that could flip the pick.
sam: yep ran that already. harness command: `python tools/microbench.py --model gpt-7b --batch 1 --seqlen 128 --repeat 50 --tile {T}`. results: 
- tile=32 no-prefetch: 9.6ms
- tile=48 prefetch-off: 9.2ms
- tile=64 prefetch-off: 9.1ms
- tile=64 prefetch-on: 12.4ms (reg spill + smem up)
elaine: wow prefetch toggles it. so kernel picker is blind to runtime prefetch toggle when deciding picks?
ryan: looks like current picker score = microbench_latency + static cost heuristics. it doesn't simulate combined smem from runtime features like kv-prefetch. we need to include runtime-feature footprints in autotuner metadata.
maria: actionable: add a dimension to kernel metadata: extra_smem_if_kv_prefetch (in bytes) and extra_regs_if_kv (if any). then autotuner scoring: est_smem = base_smem + feature_smem, compute occupancy and estimated throughput.
sam: agreed. quick patch idea: for now we can add a routing rule: if seqlen <= 160 && kv_prefetch == true -> prefer generic_tile_32 or tile_48. simple config snippet: `routing.rules += [{"cond": "seqlen<=160 and kv_prefetch", "prefer": ["generic_tile_32","generic_tile_48"]}]`
elaine: small test of that rule would be nice. can we A/B it on canary?
ryan: yeah push to canary for low-traffic customers. also add telemetry flags: record chosen_kernel, seqlen, batch, kv_prefetch. that will let us validate autotuner changes.
perf-bot: canary run summary (last 1h): rule applied on 42 requests, median latency down 14% vs default picks, p95 down 10%. trace ids: [trace:abc123, trace:def456]
maria: sweet. next step: update kernel catalog schema, add feature_smem/reg fields, and run global autotune sweep across seqlen buckets [32,64,128,256]. I'll start a PR.
sam: thanks. also keep an eye on register_spill_counter in runtime metrics — it jumped in the original regression window. if that goes down after routing rule then we found culprit. :thumbsup:
elaine: i'll roll the canary rule to the dedicated pool overnight and check dashboards tomorrow.
